security_audit.summary: Documentation-only detections are false positives, including API-key references, Markdown backticks, UUID use, and the obfuscation heuristic. The launcher still interpolates commands into shells, creates files under shared temporary paths, and directs several agents to disable approvals or sandboxing. Publication requires hardening command construction, temporary file handling, and default permission modes.

remediation.issue: Agent permission and sandbox bypasses are mandatory.
remediation.suggestion: Default every provider to sandboxed execution and normal approvals. Require explicit confirmation for each run that disables either protection.

remediation.issue: Dynamic commands and working directories are interpreted by platform shells.
remediation.suggestion: Use provider allowlists and argument arrays. Apply platform-specific quoting only where a shell is unavoidable, and remove shell=True paths.

remediation.issue: Output, marker, and executable script files use shared temporary paths.
remediation.suggestion: Create a private temporary directory with mode 0700. Create files exclusively with mode 0600, avoid symlinks, and remove files after use.

remediation.issue: Conversation history can be delegated without redaction.
remediation.suggestion: Summarize only task-relevant context, remove secrets, show the outgoing summary, and obtain confirmation before sending it to another provider.

content.user_title: Launch Coding Agents in New Terminals
content.value_statement: Starting the right coding agent requires provider-specific commands and terminal handling. This skill launches supported agents and can capture their output for later use.
actual_capabilities: Selects Claude Code by default or uses a requested supported agent.
Reads provider-specific command guidance before launching an agent.
Opens agent sessions on macOS, Windows, WSL, and Linux.
Supports interactive and non-interactive provider modes.
Captures clean agent output or full terminal debug output.
Opens provider login flows and detects common authentication failures.
limitations: The selected agent CLI must be installed and authenticated.
Terminal behavior depends on Windows Terminal, tmux, or available platform tools.
Captured output remains in temporary files until another process removes it.
Current cookbooks use broad automatic approvals that require security review.

use_cases.title: Start an Interactive Coding Session
use_cases.description: Open a separate agent terminal for implementation or repository exploration.

use_cases.title: Delegate Work With Context
use_cases.description: Send a concise conversation summary and next task to another coding agent.

use_cases.title: Compare Agent Results
use_cases.description: Run the same review task with different providers and capture their responses.

prompt_templates.title: Open the Default Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Launch Claude Code in a new terminal for this repository.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner launch without a task prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Agent and Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Spawn Gemini with the fast model in a new terminal to review the current test failures.
prompt_templates.scenario: Select a provider, model tier, and focused task.

prompt_templates.title: Delegate With a Summary
prompt_templates.prompt: Spawn Codex with a redacted summary of this conversation. Ask it to implement the agreed validation changes and capture the result.
prompt_templates.scenario: Transfer relevant context while limiting private information.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Restricted Advanced Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Launch Codex with workspace-write sandboxing and normal approvals. Review authentication handling, capture the output, and keep external network access disabled.
prompt_templates.scenario: Perform a constrained security review with explicit controls.

output_examples.input: Launch Claude Code for this repository.
output_examples.output: Claude Code opened in a new terminal using the current working directory.

output_examples.input: Spawn Gemini fast to inspect failing tests and capture its response.
output: Gemini started with the fast model.
Clean agent output will be available from the returned temporary file.

output_examples.input: Open Codex because the current provider needs authentication.
output_examples.output: A Codex login terminal opened and will report whether authentication completed before the timeout.

best_practices: Keep sandboxing and approval prompts enabled unless a reviewed task requires broader access.
Remove secrets and unrelated personal information before delegating conversation context.
Verify the working directory and delete captured output after reviewing it.
anti_patterns: Do not place untrusted prompt text inside shell commands without robust quoting.
Do not disable approvals for unknown repositories or unreviewed tasks.
Do not leave agent responses or debug logs in shared temporary directories.

faq.question: Which agents can this skill launch?
faq.answer: It includes guidance for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, and GitHub Copilot.

faq.question: Which agent is selected by default?
faq.answer: Claude Code is selected when the request names no provider.

faq.question: Which operating systems are supported?
faq.answer: The launcher contains paths for macOS, Windows, WSL, and Linux.

faq.question: Can the skill capture an agent response?
faq.answer: Yes. It can return clean agent output or full terminal debug output.

faq.question: Can it help with provider authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It can open login commands for Claude, Codex, Gemini, and Cursor.

faq.question: What security review is required before use?
faq.answer: Review permission bypass flags, shell command construction, delegated context, and temporary output handling.
